subject: Music Production
title: The Jukebox Changes Everything
description: A quick, practical guide to The Jukebox Changes Everything.

hook.text: In 1927, the Automated Musical Instrument Company placed a coin-operated phonograph in a bar.

buildup.text: Customers dropped in a nickel and picked a song, giving them control over what played.

discovery.text: Jukeboxes created massive demand for hit singles and turned unknown artists into stars overnight.

twist.text: During the Great Depression, jukeboxes thrived because a nickel was cheaper than buying a record.

climax.text: By 1940, over 300,000 jukeboxes operated across America, consuming half of all records produced.

punchline.text: A coin slot in a bar reshaped the entire music industry.

quiz.question: Why did jukeboxes thrive during the Great Depression?
options: A nickel play was cheaper than buying a record
